summary: The strongest heavy-ion-relevant item is a computationally efficient wake treatment for jet-medium response, because it targets a real bottleneck in Monte Carlo descriptions of soft jet-correlated hadrons and benchmarks against full 3+1D hydrodynamics. The day also contains useful but narrower work on light nuclei and hypernuclei at SQM 2026, non-flow multiplicity biases in RHIC-energy pp simulations, and physics-guided Gaussian processes for nuclear observables. On the AI/statistics side, the most transferable contributions concern uncertainty-aware nuclear emulation, collider jet tagging benchmarks, likelihood-combination methodology, detector-defined dataset contamination, and latent-state drift diagnosis for accelerator operations.
strongest_paper_summary: Efficient Wake model for jet-medium response, benchmarked against full 3+1D hydrodynamics and aimed at Monte Carlo jet analyses.

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Description of Medium Response to Jets in Heavy Ion Collisions
papers.short_authors: Jorge Casalderrey-Solana, Jose Guilherme Milhano, Daniel Pablos, Krishna Rajagopal, Xiaojun Yao
papers.abstract: Develops an Efficient Wake procedure for hadrons from jet wakes in heavy-ion collisions, using linearized hydrodynamics template solutions in Bjorken flow with mappings that include radial flow. The authors benchmark against full 3+1D nonlinear hydrodynamics, report reasonable agreement, and claim speedups of at least tens of thousands over full hydro.

papers.title: Production of Light Nuclei and Hypernuclei in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Reviews recent STAR and ALICE measurements of light-nucleus and hypernucleus yields, femtoscopic correlations, and collective flow from SQM 2026. The abstract emphasizes that statistical hadronization is useful but incomplete, while coalescence is broadly consistent for A<4 with sensitivity to hypertriton wave functions and feed-down treatment.

papers.title: Study of the multiplicity dependence of non-flow correlations in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=200 GeV using PYTHIA
papers.abstract: Tests the common assumption that jet-induced non-flow correlations are independent of event multiplicity by studying two-particle correlations in PYTHIA pp events at RHIC energy. The authors find non-trivial multiplicity dependence tied to biases in jet production dynamics and challenge simple LHC-style subtraction procedures at lower energy.

papers.title: Nuclear-physics-guided Gaussian Processes
papers.short_authors: Javier Rozalen Sarmiento, Hristijan Kochankovski, Arnau Rios, Angels Ramos
papers.abstract: Applies physics-guided Gaussian process regression to nucleon-nucleon phase shifts, mass excesses, and finite-temperature dense-matter equations of state. The authors report improved interpolation, uncertainty calibration, and extrapolation reliability over agnostic GP baselines, emphasizing physically motivated mean functions and kernels.

papers.title: Hunting the Unseen: Deep Learning Analysis for Semi-Visible Jet Tagging
papers.short_authors: Miguel A. Avendano-Bernal, Srinandan Dasmahapatra, Ahmed Hammad, Stefano Moretti, Mihoko Nojiri, Michael H. Seymour, Claire Shepherd-Themistocleous
papers.abstract: Benchmarks five deep-learning classifiers for semi-visible jet discrimination in Hidden Valley models, combining global event kinematics with Lund jet plane images, energy correlations, angularity, charged multiplicity, and hierarchical jet representations. Global kinematics perform strongly, while multimodal combinations give the best overall performance.

papers.title: Combinations of measurements that are simultaneous fits of parameters of interest and systematic uncertainties using the BLUE method
papers.short_authors: Tomas Dado, Mark Owen, Michele Pinamonti
papers.abstract: Extends BLUE combinations to estimates of both parameters of interest and nuisance parameters from high-statistics likelihood fits. Pseudo-experiments indicate reliable uncertainties and show that an earlier approximate likelihood-combination approach implemented in Convino can underestimate uncertainties; the method is implemented in the open-source Combiner tool.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Drift Diagnosis for Laser-Plasma Accelerator Operations
papers.short_authors: Ou Labun, Calin Hojbota, Mara Klebonas, Mike Downer, Rafal Zgadzaj, Phil Franke, Lance Labun
papers.abstract: Frames laser-plasma accelerator operations as a latent state-space model and uses an extended Kalman filter to infer effective interaction-point variables from routine beam observations. The authors test detection and attribution protocols in synthetic sessions and argue the limiting factor is the physical emission model rather than the inference algorithm.

papers.title: Prevalence Determines Precision: Silent Contamination in Detector-Defined Datasets
papers.short_authors: Jia Huang, Yankai Wan, Yangjun Ou
papers.abstract: Analyzes ML datasets constructed by detector or heuristic selection and shows that precision depends strongly on true-positive prevalence in each candidate pool. In one detector-defined event dataset, the same detector yields phantom rates ranging from 81.7% to 0.0%, and Bayes-based prevalence modeling predicts precision much better than transferring rates across pools.

cautions.title: Bayesian Superiority in On/Off analysis
cautions.abstract: Compares Bayesian criteria with flat, Jeffreys, and scale-invariant priors against the classical Li-Ma method for On/Off signal-versus-background tests. Monte Carlo studies report lower Type I and Type II error rates for Jeffreys-prior Bayesian criteria and better robustness under overdispersed backgrounds.
